text.p: Cambrex Corp said it will record a gain of $1.5 million, or $0.12 per share, in its fourth-quarter earnings as a result of a settlement it reached with the Internal Revenue Service relating to the deduction of certain intangible items in the company's 1988, 1989, 1990 and 1991 tax returns.

The company's chief financial officer, Peter Tracey, told Reuters that as a result of the gain, earnings for the quarter would be $0.12 per share higher than analysts' estimates of between $0.55 and $0.58 a share. He gave no specific figures.

The company said it agreed to pay $1.8 million in taxes and interest relating to the intangible items. It said, however, that reserves for the items were recorded on its books in previous years, resulting in the $0.12 per share gain.
The company also said it estimates its tax rate for 1997 will be about 32 percent. The company's tax rate was about 35 percent for the first three quarters of 1996, Tracey said.
Cambrex makes specialty and fine chemicals.
